question.problem: For two random variables $X$ and $Y,$ we have $\text{Var}[X]=5,$ $\text{Var}[Y]=1,$ and $\text{Cov}[X,Y]=2.$ Find $\text{Var}[2X-5Y].$

current_example.problem: For two random variables $X$ and $Y,$ we have $\textrm{Var}[X] = 5,$ $\textrm{Var}[Y] = 2,$ and $\textrm{Cov}[X,Y] = 3.$ Find $\textrm{Var}[2X - 5Y].$
current_example.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are random variables, and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

$$
\textrm{Var}[aX + bY] = a^2\textrm{Var}[X] + b^2\textrm{Var}[Y] + 2ab\,\textrm{Cov}[X,Y].
$$

Substituting the given data into the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[2X-5Y] & ={2}^{2}\cdot 5+(-5)^{2}\cdot 2+2\cdot 2\cdot (-5)\cdot 3 \\  & =20+50-60 \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$
